dataFlow.step: User signs up; email, name, phone written to SQLite users table
Booking created; name and email also written to search-index.json via BookingsIndex.add()
Account deletion sets deleted_at on the users row (soft delete); sessions and verification_codes removed immediately
Retention job deletes payments, appointments, verification_codes, sessions, users rows in SQLite for accounts whose deleted_at is older than 30 days
search-index.json is NEVER touched by the retention job — name and email remain in the JSON file indefinitely after account erasure

sinks: main-db (SQLite: users, appointments, payments, sessions, verification_codes)
search-index (JSON file: search-index.json — name, email, reason per booking)
openQuestions: The retention job purges SQLite rows but never removes entries from search-index.json. The promise is broken: name and email survive in the search index past 30 days.
SQLite DELETE without PRAGMA secure_delete=ON may leave canary bytes in freed pages; raw-bytes scan will also catch this.
